newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher, facing resistance.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher, facing resistance.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished near the day's high on Wednesday, buoyed by institutional buying on the cash market, but dealers said the index was struggling to climb higher.
Dealers said the Federal Reserve's decision to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged on Tuesday helped sentiment, but the impact was muted by overnight profit-taking on Wall Street.
"The Nikkei didn't react as positively to the Fed news as the interest rate markets. It's been struggling to get above 21,400," said Mark Falconer, sales desk manager at NatWest Futures.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract finished 10 points off its intra-day high of 21,385 against a previous settlement at 21,155. Volume was a very low 9,500 lots.

"It's hard for the Nikkei to move up when the bond market has a rocket behind it," Falconer said, adding, however that fund managers were likely to increase investments in the equity market after the Japanese fiscal half-year end next week.
"Further gains are going to be difficult until we can get above 21,500 (on the December Nikkei)," he said.
